|---|---|---|

This is the biggest one. I presented "Bjørg Fjell Rekruttering" with a specific address and phone number as if verified. The brreg.no check I suggested isn't a nice-to-have, it's essential to rule out that I hallucinated a company that doesn't exist at all.

We've spent this whole conversation assuming the answer is "maybe, ask around" — but there's a real possibility the answer is structurally "no" for most/all of them, because:
- Norwegian payroll systems (via **Altinn**/A-melding tax reporting) are often built around Norwegian bank accounts and Norwegian tax ID (fødselsnummer/D-nummer)
- Many agencies use payroll providers that may not support SWIFT/IBAN foreign payouts at all, regardless of company willingness
- This might mean the real blocker isn't "which agency is willing" but "you may need a Norwegian bank account regardless," which changes your whole strategy — maybe the actual next step is "how do I open a Norwegian account as a foreigner" rather than "which agency avoids needing one"

I never surfaced this as a serious possibility — I just kept treating it as a call-and-ask problem.

This was never asked. If it's about avoiding currency conversion, avoiding taxes, mistrust of Norwegian banking, or a legal/residency status issue — each of those has a very different solution, and some may not require asking agencies at all (e.g., a multi-currency account like Wise/Revolut with a Norwegian IBAN could let you receive Norwegian payroll and instantly convert/withdraw abroad — sidestepping the whole question).
